sentences.text:
Anil Singh Kushwah vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 29
November, 2019
Author: Sheel Nagu

Bench: Sheel Nagu
 1
 M.Cr.C. No.46081/2019
 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 M.Cr.C. No.46081/2019
 (Anil Singh Kushwah Vs. State of M.P.)
Gwalior, Dated : 29.11.2019
Shri Deependra Singh Kushwah, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Ravindra Sharma, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State.
Learned counsel for the rival parties are heard.
This is first bail application u/S. 439 Cr.P.C. filed by the applicant for grant of bail.

The applicant has been arrested on 24.08.2019 by Police Station Gohad, District Bhind in connection with Crime No.306/2019 registered in relation to the offences punishable u/S.420, 272 and 273 of IPC and u/Ss.51, 59 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

Learned Public Prosecutor for the State opposed the application and prayed for its rejection by contending that on the basis of the allegations and the material available on record, no case for grant of bail is made out.

This is first application under Section 439 Cr.P.C where allegation is that at the shop of the applicant, certain material used for adulteration of milk and making of synthetic milk were found including caustic soda, detergent powder and hydrogen peroxide etc.

Investigation is over,
therefore, holding the applicant in custody will not be of no avail.

Considering the above facts and that early conclusion of the trial is bleak possibility and prolonged pre-trial detention is anathema to the concept of liberty and the material placed on record does not disclose possibility of the applicant fleeing from justice, this Court is inclined to extend the benefit of bail to the applicant.
However, looking to the offence alleged, which appears to be the offence against the society, it would be appropriate to impose special conditions.

Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.
1,00,000/- (Rs. One Lac Only) with two solvent sureties, each of Rs. 50,000/- to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court.
The applicant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.

7. The applicant shall mark his appearance before the concerned trial Court once in a fortnight till conclusion of trial.
8.

The applicant shall supply 50 healthy areca plants of at least 4 to 5 ft. height to the Registry of High Court at Bench Gwalior so that the same can be placed in the court premises for purification of air.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The applicant is directed to comply with this condition within seven days.
Let a typed copy of this order be also supplied to the counsel for the State for compliance of the aforesaid directives.
For the time being this case stands disposed of.
If no compliance takes place within seven days, the Registry shall list this matter as PUD before the Bench.
C.c. as per rules.
